chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from Sa'd ibn Dharrīf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:

A man came to Amīr al-Mu'minīn (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Amīr al-Mu'minīn, I kiss while I am fasting.' He said to him: 'Restrain your fasting, for the beginning of the fighting is the kissing.'
And whenever a man emits semen through intimacy or speech while he is fasting, there is nothing upon him that indicates that, as he narrated:

key_terms.بَدْءَ الْقِتَالِ: The beginning of the fighting (metaphor for the start of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on kissing while fasting according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (AS) advises a fasting man who kissed while fasting to 'purify his fast,' using the metaphor that kissing is the 'beginning of the battle' against one's desires, implying it is the gateway to breaking the fast's integrity. Shia scholars interpret this as a warning against minor acts that lead to major nullifiers, emphasizing the spiritual discipline of *jihad al-nafs* (struggle against the self) during Ramadan. The concluding note clarifies that while no specific *kaffarah* (expiation) is explicitly detailed in this specific text for emission via intimacy or speech, the focus remains on the preservation of the fast's spiritual state rather than just ritual validity.
